title: Brouwer OQ-02: Fixed Point Stability and Averaged Iteration
description: Proves fixed point stability (small perturbations move fixed points by ≤ δ/(1-L)), Krasnoselskii-Mann averaged iteration T(x) = (1-t)x + tf(x) preserves the interval and reduces Lipschitz constant, and geometric decay for monotone sequences. 8 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: Stability of fixed points under perturbation is essential for computational applications: small errors in f computation lead to small errors in the fixed point. Krasnoselskii-Mann averaging (1955, 1953) stabilizes non-contractive maps.
overview.problemStatement: Prove fixed point stability under δ-perturbations and that Krasnoselskii-Mann averaging converts non-contractive maps to contractive ones.
overview.proofStrategy: Stability: |x*-y*| = |f(x*)-g(y*)| ≤ |f(x*)-g(x*)| + |g(x*)-g(y*)| ≤ δ + L|x*-y*|, giving |x*-y*| ≤ δ/(1-L). Averaging: T(x) = (1-t)x + tf(x) has Lipschitz constant (1-t+tL) = 1 - t(1-L) < 1.
keyInsights: **Perturbation bound**: |x* - y*| ≤ δ/(1-L) when g is δ-close to f. This justifies approximate oracle models in PPAD complexity.
**KM averaging**: T_t(x) = (1-t)x + tf(x) has Lipschitz 1-t(1-L). For t=1, this is the original contraction. For smaller t, it 'decelerates' convergence but handles near-contractions.
**Geometric decay**: monotone sequences bounded below decrease geometrically toward their infimum — the abstract template for convergence proofs.

sections.title: Stability Under Perturbation and Averaged Iteration
sections.summary: fixed_point_stability: |x*-y*| ≤ δ/(1-L). km_iteration_self_map. km_lipschitz: Lip(T_t) = 1-t(1-L). geometric_decay_lemma.

conclusion.summary: 8 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms. Fixed point stability and Krasnoselskii-Mann averaging proved.
conclusion.implications: These stability results justify the oracle model for approximate Brouwer computation: approximating f within δ is sufficient to find the fixed point within ε.
openQuestions: Can Krasnoselskii-Mann convergence for firmly non-expansive maps be formalized?
Can the Halpern iteration be proved to converge strongly?
Can the Douglas-Rachford splitting be verified?
